verses.text: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became king in his place.

David said, "I will be kind to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father was kind to me." So David sent some of his officials to comfort Hanun about his father's death. When David's officials arrived in the land of the Ammonites,

the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun their master, "Do you really think David is honouring your father by sending men to comfort you? No! David has sent them to look around the city, to spy on it, and then destroy it."
So Hanun took David's officials, shaved off half of each man's beard, cut their clothes off in the middle at their buttocks, and sent them away.
When David was told about this, he sent messengers to meet them, because the men were deeply ashamed. The king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then come home."

The Ammonites realised that they had made David their enemy. So they sent and hired twenty thousand Syrian foot soldiers from Beth Rehob and Zobah, the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and twelve thousand men from Tob.
When David heard about it, he sent Joab with the whole army of his best fighting men.
The Ammonites came out and got ready for battle at the entrance to their city gate. The Syrians from Zobah and Rehob and the men from Tob and Maacah stayed by themselves in the open field.
Joab saw that there were enemy troops in front of him and behind him. So he chose some of the best soldiers in Israel and lined them up to face the Syrians.
He put the rest of the men under the command of his brother Abishai, who lined them up to face the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, you must come and help me. But if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will come and help you.
Be brave! Let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. And may the LORD do what he thinks is best."
So Joab and his men moved forward to fight the Syrians, and the Syrians ran away from him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Syrians were running away, they also ran from Abishai and went back into their city. Then Joab returned from fighting the Ammonites and came back to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians saw that Israel had defeated them, they gathered together again.
Hadadezer sent for the Syrians who lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they came to Helam. Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
When David was told about this, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and came to Helam. The Syrians lined up to face David and fought against him.
But the Syrians ran away from Israel. David killed seven hundred Syrian chariot drivers and forty thousand horsemen. He also struck down Shobach, the commander of their army, and he died there.
All the kings who served Hadadezer saw that Israel had defeated them, so they made peace with Israel and became their servants. After that, the Syrians were afraid to help the Ammonites any more.
